result.prompt: Use a new paper boat for each sample weighing.
Count sonication time only after the sonicator starts.
A short sonicator cycle can run with a low water level.
Keep different-sized flasks 2cm apart in the sonicator.
Clean the analytical balance pan with a brush before use.
After pressing Start, check that the sonicator is working.
If weighing the same chemical, a boat paper can be reused.
Label the glassware with the sample details before weighing.
Flasks can touch inside the sonicator if held firmly in place.
Stopping the sonicator once the sample dissoves will save time
Check the calibration register before using analytical balance.
Check the sonicator water level after placing the flasks inside.
Replace contaminated sonicator bath water even if it looks clean.
Place the paper boat at the centre of the analytical balance pan.
A gap between sonicator flasks is needed only for different samples.
The paper boat need not be centred if the balance reading is stable.
Use a STP specified flask size in the sonicator to avoid overfilling.
Adding fresh water makes contaminated sonicator water suitable for reuse
If only one sample is weighed, glassware can be labelled after weighing.
Extra sonicator time can make up for missed intermittent shaking of flask.
Check the analytical balance for any residue, even if the pan looks clean.
Check that the analytical balance’s levelling bubble is centred before use.
Zero (tare) the analytical balance with a new, empty paper boat on the pan.
Hand shake the flask as required, even when the sonicator runs continuously.
If the balance reading is stable, the leveling bubble need not be in centre.
To save time, a sonicator temperature slightly above the STP limit is acceptable.
Check sonicator bath temperature, even if the previous batch used the same setting.
Samples can be shaken by hand for the same duration if the sonicator is unavailable.
If the solution looks clear, required intermittent shaking in sonicator can be skipped.
If the reading in analytical balance is zero, checking its calibration status can be skipped.
For sonication, the smaller flask can be filled above the allowed level to fit a larger sample.
